title: Adjoints and small localizations of presentable infinity categories
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be presentable infinity categories, meaning accessible infinity categories admitting all small colimits, with sizes fixed in nested universes as in [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. They admit all small limits. A functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ has a right adjoint if and only if it preserves small colimits. For any small set $S$ of arrows in $\mathcal C$, the full subcategory of objects $Z$ such that $\operatorname{Map}(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $(A\to B)\in S$ is presentable and its inclusion has an accessible left adjoint. Its limits are computed in $\mathcal C$ and its colimits are obtained by applying that left adjoint to the colimits in $\mathcal C$. Adjunctions here are mapping-space adjunctions with coherent units, counits and triangle identities.

source.place: Corollaries 5.5.2.4 and 5.5.2.9, Proposition 5.5.4.15, and section 5.2.7 Read online where available; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text:
Let $p:J\to\mathcal C$ be any small coherent diagram. In the space-valued presheaf category form $H=\lim_{j\in J}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(-,p(j))$, using [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Its values are small spaces. For $c=\operatorname{colim}_{k\in K}q(k)$ the same node gives
$$H(c)\simeq\lim_j\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(q(k),p(j))\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}H(q(k)).$$
The second equivalence just interchanges two small limits: a cone to either iterated limit is the same compatible family indexed by $J\times K^{\mathrm{op}}$. Thus [lem-coef-infinity-continuous-presheaf-representability] represents $H$ by an object $l$. Under the fully faithful Yoneda functor the projections $H\to\operatorname{Map}(-,p(j))$ give a coherent cone $l\to p$, and its tested mapping spaces are exactly $H(x)$. The cone criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] proves it limiting. This proves existence of all small limits, including the terminal object when $J$ is empty, for every presentable infinity category, in particular both $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$. No limit indexed by the large category $\mathcal C$ is taken.

source.place: Corollary 5.5.2.4, using Proposition 5.5.2.2 and infinity Yoneda

proof.text:
If $F$ preserves small colimits, then for each $d\in\mathcal D$ the presheaf $H_d(c)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(F(c),d)$ carries small colimits to limits by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. By [lem-coef-infinity-continuous-presheaf-representability] it is representable. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion] to assemble these representations into a right adjoint with its coherent adjunction. Conversely, if $F\dashv R$, and $c=\operatorname{colim}_Jq$, the adjunction and the mapping-space colimit criterion give, naturally in $d$,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(F(c),d)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,Rd)\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(q(j),Rd)\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Fq(j),d).$$
These are the maps of the image cocone, so the same criterion proves that $F(c)$ is its colimit. The argument includes the empty diagram.

Fix the small set $S$ in the statement, and let $W$ be its replete strongly saturated closure as defined in [lem-coef-small-saturated-coslice-presentability]. For an $S$-local object $Z$, let $E_Z$ be the arrows inverted by $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(-,Z)$. It contains equivalences and has two-out-of-three. Pushouts go to homotopy pullbacks, so pushing out a member still gives a member. For a small diagram of arrows in $E_Z$, its source and target colimits are computed objectwise in the arrow category by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Mapping these colimits into $Z$ gives the limits of a coherent transformation of space-valued diagrams whose components are equivalences. This transformation is an equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]; applying the limit functor carries it and its inverse to inverse maps. Thus the colimit arrow still belongs to $E_Z$. Therefore $E_Z$ is strongly saturated and contains $S$, whence $W\subset E_Z$. Conversely $S\subset W$. Thus $S$-local and $W$-local mean exactly the same condition. This is a closure argument, not an additional localization theorem.

For each $X\in\mathcal C$, [lem-coef-small-saturated-coslice-presentability] makes the full coherent coslice category $\mathcal D_X$ of arrows $X\to Y$ in $W$ presentable: its hypotheses are precisely presentability of $\mathcal C$ and smallness of $S$. Step 1, now applied to $\mathcal D_X$ and the empty diagram, gives a final object $s:X\to Y$ of $\mathcal D_X$. We use this finality only inside the full subcategory on $W$, retaining all triangle homotopies.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.5.14, first paragraph, using Lemma 5.5.4.14, Proposition 5.4.6.6 and Lemma 5.5.4.12

proof.text:
We prove that the target $Y$ of $s$ is $W$-local. Take $t:A\to B$ in $W$ and any $g:A\to Y$. Form the pushout $Z=Y\amalg_A B$ and its arrow $t':Y\to Z$, which is in $W$. Its composite $s'=t's:X\to Z$ is also in $W$. Fullness and finality of $s$ make both $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_{X/}}(s',s)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_{X/}}(s,s)$ contractible. Composition with the triangle $s\to s'$ is consequently an equivalence between these spaces, and its homotopy fiber at $1_s$ is contractible by [lem-coef-space-contractible-fiber-equivalence].

By the dual coslice mapping-space formula of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], the two spaces above are respectively $\operatorname{Map}(Z,Y)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}(X,Y)}\{s\}$ and $\operatorname{Map}(Y,Y)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}(X,Y)}\{s\}$. Composition with the triangle is the base change of $t'^*:\operatorname{Map}(Z,Y)\to\operatorname{Map}(Y,Y)$. Its fiber at $1_s$ is therefore the fiber of $t'^*$ at $1_Y$, simply by associating the homotopy pullbacks. The same dual formula identifies this with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_{Y/}}(t',1_Y)$; it specifies a map $q:Z\to Y$ and the homotopy $qt'\simeq1_Y$ with all its higher data. The pushout mapping-space formula of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] identifies that fiber with the fiber at $g$ of $\operatorname{Map}(B,Y)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,Y)$: mapping out of $Z$ is the pullback of the two mapping spaces over $\operatorname{Map}(A,Y)$. Every such fiber is thus contractible. All these mapping spaces are Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], so [lem-coef-space-contractible-fiber-equivalence] proves the latter map an equivalence. This holds for every $t$ and $g$; hence $Y$ is $W$-local, including when the space of $g$ is empty.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.5.14, remainder of proof; its Lemmas 5.5.5.12 and 5.5.5.13 are obtained here by the cited general cone formula and the pushout universal property; Kerodon Remark 3.4.0.6 for the fiber criterion

proof.text: Let $\mathcal E$ be the replete full subcategory of $S$-local objects, equivalently of $W$-local objects by step 3. The construction of steps 4 and 5 gives $s_X:X\to Y_X$ in $W$ with $Y_X\in\mathcal E$. For every $Z\in\mathcal E$, precomposition with $s_X$ is a natural equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(Y_X,Z)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(Y_X,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(X,iZ)$, exactly because $Z$ is $W$-local. The dual criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion] supplies a coherent left adjoint $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ to the inclusion $i$. Its units agree, up to equivalences in the coherent coslices, with the universal maps $s_X$; in particular every unit $\eta_X:X\to iLX$ is in $W$. This invokes representability of covariant mapping-space functors on $\mathcal E$, not the presentable adjoint theorem before $\mathcal E$ is known presentable.

Let $q:J\to\mathcal E$ be small. Its limit $l=\lim_J iq$ exists in $\mathcal C$ by step 1. For $A\to B$ in $S$, [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] identifies $\operatorname{Map}(B,l)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,l)$ with the limit of the equivalences $\operatorname{Map}(B,iq(j))\to\operatorname{Map}(A,iq(j))$. The pointwise equivalence criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes that transformation an equivalence of space-valued diagrams; the limit functor carries its inverse to an inverse for the displayed map. Thus $l$ is local; fullness and the same mapping-space criterion give the limit in $\mathcal E$. For colimits put $c=\operatorname{colim}_J iq$ in $\mathcal C$. For every $Z\in\mathcal E$ the adjunction gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(Lc,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,iZ)\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(q(j),Z).$$
The colimit criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] proves $Lc=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal E}q$. Both formulas include empty diagrams, proving in particular that $\mathcal E$ has all small colimits.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.4.15 and the mapping-space universal properties of limits and colimits

proof.text: Let $T$ be all arrows inverted by $iL$. If $f:A\to B$ belongs to $W$, precomposition gives an equivalence of mapping spaces into every local $Z$ by step 3. The adjunction identifies these maps with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(LB,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(LA,Z)$, so the fully faithful Yoneda functor for $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] detects that $Lf$ is an equivalence. Thus $W\subset T$. Conversely, for $f\in T$ the coherent naturality square $iL(f)\eta_A\simeq\eta_B f$ has both units in $W$ by step 6, and $iL(f)$ is an equivalence, hence lies in $W$. Two-out-of-three gives $f\in W$. Therefore $T=W$, and its local objects are exactly the $S$-local objects by step 3. The coherence of this square is part of the units supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion].

source.place: Proposition 5.5.4.15(4), using the mapping-space universal property of the reflector

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-reflector-accessibility] to the adjunction already constructed. The source $\mathcal C$ is accessible since it is presentable; $\mathcal E$ is replete and full; and the small set $S_0=S$ lies in $T=W$ by step 8 and detects all $T$-local objects by step 3. The criterion proves that $\mathcal E$ and $iL$ are accessible. Step 7 supplies all small colimits, so $\mathcal E$ is presentable. Finally $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ preserves all small colimits: for any small $q:J\to\mathcal C$, adjunction and the colimit criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] give $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(L\operatorname{colim}q,Z)\simeq\lim_{J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(Lq(j),Z)$. It therefore preserves small $\kappa$-filtered colimits for every regular $\kappa$; its source and target are accessible, so it is accessible. The adjunctions in steps 2 and 6 already have the units, counits and coherent triangle identities furnished by the pointwise adjoint criterion; no passage to homotopy categories is used.

split_report.summary: Kept the statement. Gave nine steps constructing small limits by space-valued representability, proving the adjoint criterion, and constructing small-set local replacements by final objects in strongly saturated coherent coslices. Proved locality through explicit homotopy fibers, then the reflector, limit/colimit formulas, inverted-arrow classification and accessibility. Six new statement-only foundational nodes; ordinary-category Mathlib analogues are not infinity-category results. Reused the existing enhanced cone calculus rather than duplicate its coslice mapping-space formula. Second reading makes the pointwise-equivalence citations explicit, tightens the strong-saturation source, and marks all nine substantive steps non-elementary.
split_report.blueprint: Main-20261015 prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint proof paragraph 2: the finite-coefficient mapping-complex adjunction and the subsequent R lim require coherent adjoints and limits; this is foundational infrastructure reached through the existing enriched-calculus chain, not a replacement for its derived-section computation.

tool_uses.why: Its coherent coslice mapping-space fiber formula and Kan property identify the two finality mapping spaces as homotopy pullbacks, and identify the fiber over the identity in the locality proof; our unit has no such general quasicategory formula. This is a foundational tool, not a replacement for a coefficient or purity route. Its pointwise-equivalence criterion also justifies the transformations of space-valued diagrams in steps 3 and 7.
